description: Reviewed dated discrete-plate directional evidence and mill developments. Survey-based readings are identified with limitations; other metrics remain unverified until comparable plate-specific evidence is available.

observations.basis: Steel Market Update described continued limited availability of plate alongside longer lead times and rising plate prices. This is a report of spot-market scarcity, not a measured week-over-week change in national plate output.
observations.limitation: Qualitative supply-pressure indicator; current shortage does not necessarily establish additional tightening. Source overlaps the pricing observation, so these are not independent confirmations.
observations.verification: Reviewed dated industry reporting on plate availability; directional assessment limited to reported spot-market pressure.

source.title: SMU Price Ranges rise on tight supply, no signs of a year-end slowdown

observations.basis: Steel Market Update reported that sheet and plate prices continued to move higher amid limited availability and extended lead times. The direction refers specifically to reported plate price movement, not the hot-rolled coil price cited elsewhere in the article.
observations.limitation: Qualitative published plate-price trend; no verified A36/A572-50/A516-70 transaction price or independent dollar-per-cwt benchmark. Expires after 21 days.
observations.verification: Dated plate-specific price direction explicitly stated in published industry reporting.

source.title: SMU Price Ranges rise on tight supply, no signs of a year-end slowdown

observations.basis: SMU's late-October buyer survey reported that sheet and plate mill lead times continued to lengthen; plate exceeded its 2021 peak and set a record for its survey series beginning in 2018. Its October 16 report placed average plate lead times at 11 weeks.
observations.limitation: Survey-based U.S. market trend, not a guaranteed lead time from any specific plate mill, grade or thickness. The 11-week average was reported October 16, not October 29. Evidence expires after 21 days unless a newer plate-specific survey confirms direction.
observations.verification: Reviewed SMU reporting; late-October survey described explicitly increasing plate lead times.

source.title: Mill lead times climb to new highs, buyers expect little relief

observations.basis: SMU reported shrinking remaining 2026 domestic spot tonnage for plate and sheet, with steel buyers struggling to find domestic mills offering spot availability. This indicates tightening spot access, not a measured decline in total U.S. plate production.
observations.limitation: Qualitative buyer reports; cannot infer exact mill allocation percentages or all-grade availability. Supply direction here refers to domestic spot-order availability.
observations.verification: Reviewed SMU late-October reporting on domestic plate spot availability.

source.title: Sheet and plate price gains accelerate as 2026 tons dry up

observations.basis: Steel Market Update attributed the domestic plate squeeze partly to improved plate demand, alongside tariffs and planned outages. This is a qualitative September directional assessment, not a measured October/November plate-order index.
observations.limitation: Low confidence: qualitative analyst assessment from September, not a current plate-specific demand series. Supply restrictions can magnify apparent demand strength.
observations.verification: Published plate-specific industry analysis explicitly attributes the squeeze to improved demand.

source.title: Plate feels the squeeze, outages well underway

market_developments.summary: AISI reported October 2026 cut-length plate import permits 34% above September final imports. This compares permit applications with prior-month actual imports; it does not prove actual October arrivals, current availability, or a sustained trend.
market_developments.limitation: Do not score Import Availability from this single mixed-basis comparison. Confirm subsequent cut-length plate arrivals and consistent month-to-month series.

source.title: AISI Releases October SIMA Imports Data

market_developments.summary: AISI reported August cut-length plate import permits rose 72% versus July final imports. Permits are intended tonnage, not confirmed arrivals or currently available plate. September broad steel imports do not establish a later cut-length plate trend.
market_developments.limitation: Do not infer import availability is improving from permits alone; check subsequent cut-length plate arrivals and comparable permit data.

source.title: AISI Releases August SIMA Imports Data

mill_developments.summary: A public report quoting JSW’s CEO described a planned 45-day Baytown plate-mill outage starting in September for upgrades. Completion and present production status have not been verified; the scheduled duration is not a restart confirmation.
mill_developments.status: Historical reported plan; current status unverified

source.publisher: Steel Market Update, quoting JSW management
source.title: JSW Steel USA moves 45-day outage to September

mill_developments.date_kind: reporting period end; changes described in the Q3 10-Q
mill_developments.summary: The Q3 2026 filing describes idling the Gary plate finishing line and one Burns Harbor plate mill during Q2, consolidating capabilities at one Burns Harbor mill. The company said capability and steel output were not compromised. This is a dated footprint change, not proof of current spot availability or allocations.
mill_developments.verification_anchor: idling our Gary plate finishing line
mill_developments.status: Dated company filing; current availability unverified
